name: Sea Bonze (Mythic)
body:
Mythic Sea Bonze
CR 19/MR 7

Massive and blacker than the darkest depths of the sea, this colossal watery form glares with two immense, hate-filled eyes.

XP 204,800
NE Gargantuan undead (aquatic, mythic)
Init +11/-9, dual initiative; Senses blindsight 120 ft., mistsight, see in darkness; Perception +33

DEFENSE

AC 37, touch 6, flat-footed 37 (+31 natural, –4 size)
hp 287 (22d8+188)
Fort +19 Ref +15 Will +25
Defensive Abilities elusive, unholy grace; DR 10/epic and magic and slashing; Immune cold, electricity, undead traits; Resist acid 10, fire 10

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., swim 80 ft.
Melee 2 slams +25 (4d10+13 plus draining strike)
Space 20 ft.; Reach 20 ft.
Special Attacks capsize (DC 35), dooming gaze (60 ft., DC 27), draining strike, mythic power (7/day, surge +1d10), simple divine spellcasting
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 22nd; concentration +28)

1/day—antilife shell, commune with nature, control water (none or DC 20), control weather, control winds (DC 21), protection from energy, storm of vengeance (none or DC 25)

STATISTICS

Str 36, Dex 11, Con —, Int 13, Wis 18, Cha 23
Base Atk +16; CMB +33; CMD 43 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Alertness, Blind-Fight, Combat Reflexes, Critical Focus, Improved Initiative, Improved Iron Will, Intimidating Prowess, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Stand Still, Vital StrikeMF
Skills Intimidate +44, Perception +33, Sense Motive +33, Stealth +13, Swim +50; Racial Modifiers +4 Swim
Languages Aquan, Common

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Cursed Wound (Su)

The damage a mythic sea bonze deals doesn’t heal naturally and resists magical healing. A character attempting to use magical healing on a creature damaged by a mythic sea bonze must succeed on a DC 27 caster level check, or the healing has no effect on the injured creature.

Dooming Gaze (Su)

Paralyzed with fear for 1 round, 60 feet Will DC 27 negates. A creature that is already paralyzed by this gaze attack and fails a saving throw to resist being paralyzed for 1 more round gains 1 negative level (Fortitude DC 27 to remove after 24 hours). The paralysis effect of this gaze is a mind-affecting fear effect, but the negative level is not. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Draining Strike (Su)

A living creature struck by a mythic sea bonze’s slam attack takes 3d6 points of negative energy damage. Alternatively, the sea bonze can choose to make the target fatigued for 1 hour or shaken for 1 minute rather than dealing this negative energy damage. If the target is a mythic creature, the sea bonze can instead drain one use of its mythic power; it can then use that mythic power itself but must use it before the end of its next turn or it is lost.

A mythic sea bonze may expend one use of mythic power as a free action to inflict one negative level on the target (DC 27 to remove). It can expend more than one use of mythic power if it wishes, inflicting one negative level for each use of mythic power it expends. If the hit is a critical hit, it inflicts two negative levels for each use of mythic power it expends.

Elusive (Su)

A mythic sea bonze has long been the stuff of maritime legends, but despite countless attempts to hunt them, they are rarely encountered unless they wish it. As a full-round action while in water, the mythis sea bonze can move up to its run speed (400 ft.) without leaving any trace of its passing (identical in effect to a pass without trace spell). The mythic sea bonze gains a +40 circumstance bonus to its Stealth check. In addition, except when in combat, the creature is considered to be under the effects of a nondetection spell. Both of these spell effects are at caster level 20th and cannot be dispelled.

Unholy Grace (Su)

A mythic sea bonze adds its Charisma modifier as a profane bonus on all its saving throws (bonus included above).

ECOLOGY

Environment any oceans
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Sea bonzes are formed from the combined despair and horror of death at sea, such as when a ship sinks and its entire crew drowns. No single restless soul empowers a sea bonze—it combines the anger and doom of all who die in such close proximity.
